Ransomware Attack Disrupts Luxembourg Steel Sector, Operations Restored

A sophisticated ransomware attack targeting Luxembourg’s steel industry forced a temporary shutdown of IT systems at several leading firms, including ArcelorMittal SA, last week. The incident, which began late last Friday, led to the suspension of certain production lines and delays in order processing across the sector.

According to the Luxembourg Steel Federation, the attack exploited vulnerabilities in remote access software used by multiple companies. In addition to ArcelorMittal SA, local steelmaker LuxForge Industries also reported disruptions. The attackers allegedly encrypted critical data and demanded payment in cryptocurrency to restore access.

The incident prompted immediate coordination with Luxembourg’s national cybersecurity agency, which assisted in isolating affected networks and mitigating the spread. “We acted swiftly to contain the breach and prevent further escalation,” said Marie Thill, Chief Information Security Officer at ArcelorMittal SA. “Our priority was to protect our employees and partners while restoring operations as quickly and safely as possible.”

ArcelorMittal SA confirmed in a statement on Tuesday that its IT teams, working with external cybersecurity specialists, had successfully restored core systems over the weekend. Production resumed at all Luxembourg facilities by Monday morning, though some administrative functions remain under enhanced monitoring. “We have restored operations and are implementing further safeguards to strengthen our resilience,” Thill added.

The federation estimates the attack caused a temporary loss of up to 25% in output at affected mills, with knock-on effects on delivery schedules. “Our members are working overtime to clear the backlog and assure customers of continued supply,” said Jacques Muller, General Secretary of the Luxembourg Steel Federation.

Industry analysts noted that the incident highlights the increasing digital risks faced by heavy industry. “Steel producers are investing heavily in automation and digital platforms, but this also increases their exposure to cyber threats,” said Sophie Bernard, a sector analyst at Banque du Luxembourg. “Companies will need to double down on security to avoid future disruptions.”

Union representatives have called for further investment in cybersecurity training and infrastructure to protect jobs and critical industrial operations.
